subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the levels of organisation, smallest to largest?
questions.explain: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, organs make organ systems.

questions.q: What is the function of ribosomes?
questions.explain: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.

questions.q: One disadvantage of selective breeding is that it:
options: Can reduce genetic variation, increasing the risk of disease
questions.explain: Selective breeding reduces variation (inbreeding), making organisms more vulnerable to disease.

questions.q: Genetic engineering involves:
options: Breeding two organisms over many generations
Transferring a gene from one organism into another
Exposing organisms to sunlight to change genes
questions.explain: Genetic engineering transfers genes from one organism into another, e.g. inserting a human gene into bacteria.

questions.q: What is the function of the cell wall in a plant cell?
options: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explain: The plant cell wall is made of cellulose and provides strength and support.

questions.q: Why did it take a long time for Darwin's theory to be widely accepted?
options: No one was interested in biology
It conflicted with religious beliefs and the mechanism of inheritance was not yet known
questions.explain: Darwin's theory challenged religious views and lacked a known mechanism of inheritance (genes were not yet understood).

questions.q: Which part of a bacterial cell can carry extra genes, for example genes for antibiotic resistance?
questions.explain: Plasmids are small rings of DNA, separate from the main chromosome, that can carry extra genes such as for antibiotic resistance.

questions.q: A cell appears 40 mm wide under a microscope at a magnification of ×400. What is its actual width?
questions.explain: Actual size = image size ÷ magnification = 40 ÷ 400 = 0.1 mm.

questions.q: The rapid emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is evidence for evolution because:
options: Resistant bacteria survive antibiotics and reproduce, so resistance spreads
Antibiotics create resistant bacteria from nothing
questions.explain: Resistant bacteria survive and reproduce by natural selection, demonstrating evolution happening quickly.

questions.q: Which statement about light microscopes compared with electron microscopes is correct?
options: Light microscopes can show the inside detail of organelles clearly
Light microscopes are cheaper and can view living specimens
Light microscopes use beams of electrons to form an image
Light microscopes have higher magnification and resolution
questions.explain: Light microscopes are cheaper and can be used to look at living cells, but have lower magnification and resolution than electron microscopes.

questions.q: In the binomial naming system, an organism is named using its:
questions.explain: Binomial names use the genus (first, capitalised) and species (second), e.g. Homo sapiens.

questions.q: A farmer breeds the cows that produce the most milk together over many generations. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Choosing parents with a desired trait (high milk yield) to breed together over generations is selective breeding.

questions.q: A sperm cell has many mitochondria. What is this an adaptation for?
options: Providing energy for the tail to swim to the egg
questions.explain: The many mitochondria release energy for the flagellum (tail) to swim to the egg.

questions.q: Studying the genome (DNA) of organisms has improved classification because it:
options: Proves that all species are identical
Replaces the need for naming organisms
Shows how closely related species are by comparing their DNA
questions.explain: Comparing DNA reveals evolutionary relationships, leading to changes such as the three-domain classification system.

questions.q: An image of a cell is 30 mm long and the magnification is ×1500. What is the actual size?
questions.explain: Actual = image ÷ magnification = 30 mm ÷ 1500 = 0.02 mm = 20 µm.

questions.q: Why do fossils provide incomplete evidence for evolution?
options: Many soft-bodied organisms decayed without forming fossils, leaving gaps in the record
Fossils cannot be dated at all
Fossils are too recent to be useful
questions.explain: Many early or soft-bodied organisms left no fossils, so the fossil record has gaps and is incomplete.

questions.q: Extinction occurs when:
options: A species temporarily moves to a new area
A species becomes endangered but survives
No individuals of a species remain alive anywhere
questions.explain: Extinction is when there are no remaining individuals of a species left alive.

questions.q: Which of these could cause a species to become extinct?
options: A new predator or disease and loss of habitat
questions.explain: New predators, disease, habitat destruction or environmental change can all drive a species to extinction.

questions.q: How can the development of antibiotic resistance be slowed down?
options: Only prescribing antibiotics when needed and finishing the full course
Not finishing the full course of antibiotics
questions.explain: Reducing unnecessary use and always completing the course helps stop resistant bacteria surviving and spreading.

questions.q: A xylem vessel cell is hollow and has no living contents and no end walls. This adapts it to:
questions.explain: Hollow, dead xylem cells joined end to end form continuous tubes for water transport.

questions.q: Which is a real example of genetic engineering?
options: Dogs bred for a calm temperament
Bacteria modified to produce human insulin
questions.explain: Bacteria can be genetically modified to make human insulin, used to treat diabetes.

questions.q: Which of these is the smallest and would need the highest magnification to be seen?
questions.explain: A mitochondrion is a sub-cellular organelle and is smaller than a whole bacterium or animal cell.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology (4BI1) specification; Nature Variety Of Living Organisms
